question: What is the value of \[ \begin{gathered} \log_3 7\cdot\log_5 9\cdot\log_7 11 \\ {}\cdot\log_9 13\cdots\log_{21} 25\cdot\log_{23} 27? \end{gathered} \]
solution:
Changing every logarithm to the same base exposes matching factors that cancel. Write \(P\) for the requested product, and use base-ten logarithms in the change-of-base formula:
\[
\log_a b=\frac{\log b}{\log a}.
\]
Thus
\[
P=\frac{\log 7\,\log 9\,\log 11\cdots\log 25\,\log 27}
{\log 3\,\log 5\,\log 7\cdots\log 21\,\log 23}.
\]
Every factor \(\log 7,\log 9,\ldots,\log 23\) occurs once in both the numerator and denominator, so these factors cancel. Therefore
\[
P=\frac{\log 25\,\log 27}{\log 3\,\log 5}
=\frac{(2\log 5)(3\log 3)}{\log 3\,\log 5}
=6.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{6}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
